title: test(runtime): judge each share-link password pair once in the messages-audience file
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-sales"} -->
_Requested by **Sales** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4Uu?thread=cmsg_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4UuDWJsBGQpadCH8JR2xZQ5re)_

Part of #23181 (slice 7). The card stays open for later slices.
Clause-②: no

## What changes

One test file: `packages/runtime/src/domains/share-links-messages-audience.test.ts`. Its `beforeAll` wraps the `ShareLinkService` instance's own password verifier in a memo keyed by the `(password, hash)` pair. This is the same memo `share-links-refusal-order.test.ts` beside it got in PR #24704. The first request that presents a pair is judged by the production verifier (scrypt at the account parameters). Every later request with that pair gets the same verdict back.

What stays the same:
- every request is still made, on both mounts and both routes, so every answer is still a real request's answer;
- every row, case and assertion: 85 tests before, 85 after;
- the service is still built with both password members at their defaults, as production builds it;
- if `verifyPassword` stops being the member name, `beforeAll` throws instead of quietly going back to paying for every call.

## Measured (local, shared box, `origin/main` `830a63a680` vs this head `6e979387cc`)

Each run is `pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/domains/share-links-messages-audience.test.ts` under `os-verify-lock`. The box is shared, so the ratios are the reading to trust, not the absolute numbers.

| | run 1 | run 2 | run 3 |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|
| per-file duration before (json reporter, the unit CI's module line reports) | 3695 ms | 3816 ms | 3580 ms |
| per-file duration after | 891 ms | 928 ms | 864 ms |
| vitest `Duration` before (wall incl. ~15 s import) | 19.30 s | 18.93 s | 18.89 s |
| vitest `Duration` after | 16.80 s | 17.98 s | 17.79 s |

- scrypt derivations, counted with a measurement-only preload that wraps `node:crypto.scrypt` (not part of this PR): **32 before** (30 verifier calls + 2 password mints), **6 after** (4 distinct pairs + 2 mints), the same in all three after-runs. Before, the derivations added up to 3817 ms, which is about the whole per-file duration.
- Per-file ratio after/before: about 0.24. Applied to the card's CI reading (13.51 s, run `39298888283`), that projects to about 3.3 s, under the 10 s line. The next refresh's list is the real check.
- The rest of the wall is module import (~15 s), and it is the same before and after. The per-file reading the card grades does not count import time.

## Tests and gates (at `6e979387cc`)

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime test`: Test Files 438 passed (438), Tests 7022 passed / 19 skipped; lock VERDICT command-exit 0.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime typecheck`: lock VERDICT command-exit 0, test layer included (`check:test-typecheck: OK`).
- `pnpm lint`: exit 0.
- `dispatch-gates --commands` derived 54 commands. 53 exited 0. `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads` exited 3, PREREQUISITE NOT MET (it needs every package's `dist/`, and this worktree built only the runtime closure), so it is NOT MEASURED here. CI's Lint & Repo Gates runs it. `--ran`: 54 accounted, 53 run, 1 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN.

## Changeset

`skip-changeset`: the only change is a `*.test.ts` file. `@objectstack/runtime` ships `files: [dist, README.md, CHANGELOG.md]`, and Build Core checks that no compiled test file ends up in any dist.

## Acceptance notes

- The dispatch suggested importing PR #24704's memo instead of copying it. That memo is written inline in the sibling file's `beforeAll` and is not exported, so it can only be imported after being moved into a shared testkit. Doing that touches the sibling file and adds a new file, which is outside this slice's one-file surface. So the same 13 lines are copied here, and the comment names the sibling. Moving both copies into a `share-link-verifier-memo.testkit.ts` would be a small follow-up for whoever owns this lane.
